steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Combine milk, brown sugar, cornstarch, and salt in the top of a double boiler over simmering water. Cook, stirring constantly, until mixture starts to thicken, about 20 minutes.
Whisk in egg yolks; cook and stir until filling is thickened. Remove filling from heat; stir in butter and vanilla.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top begins to brown, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Butterscotch Pie
raw_recipe.description: This butterscotch pie has a homemade creamy butterscotch filling made with brown sugar, milk, and eggs for a sweet holiday dessert with old-fashioned flavor.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma's Butterscotch Pie

review.reviewBody: I've been spreading the word about this recipe! If you don't have a double boiler, don't worry. It will still work just fine (I used medium heat and stirred constantly!) Tastes great with whipped cream on top.

The bad news: if butterscotch is your thing, this could be slightly dangerous! The good news: I was able to make this almost dairy free by using cashew milk. Also, the microwave method works!! I mixed my cornstarch and brown sugar really well, eliminating any lumps, then slowly whisked in my milk before putting it in the micro. Left it in there undisturbed for eight minutes and it was a thickened dream! Soooo good!

This came out better then I thought it would. I don't have a double boiler so I just did what my grandma said do, fill a frying pan with water then set the pot over in it and cook that way. I will say that this is definitely a pie you can not walk away from. when it says stir constantly it basically means the whole 20.minutes, lol. I did just that because I have watched my mom make lemon meringue pie or rice pudding and the key has always been the constant stirring. it also takes way longer then 5 minutes to brown, at least mine did. I noticed that it started to set after about 15 minutes but still needed a little more to go.

I've made this a couple of times in the past. Always turns out well. It's my niece's favorite pie that I make and since I was going to her house for Christmas dinner, I made it and another pie as my contribution to the meal. The only thing I do differently is to whisk in the egg yolks with the milk and brown sugar at the very beginning and add the butter and vanilla at the end. Always turns out well.

This was absolutely delightful, and easy to make once I figured out how thick "until it thickens" meant. I also cooked it over the stove gently, instead of using a double boiler. Easy peasy. My boyfriend and I both loved it- We made it because of the game "Undertale" which has a butterscotch cinnamon pie in it, so I added a dash of cinnamon to the pie itself, and made whipped cream with cinnamon to top each slice.

I thought the taste of the filling was nice. It's slightly sweeter than any homemade butterscotch I've had. It seemed to take forever to thicken over a double boiler. I think next time I'll just take care and just use direct/indirect heat whisking constantly. I found it didn't thicken as much as I would have liked. It's my first time making it and I will make it again to get it right. Thank you.

This was a yummy basic recipe. I made the following changes; used dark brown sugar for a richer color and taste and made a pretzel crust to help balance the sweetness of the filling. I also made a lightly sweetened vanilla bean whipped cream topping. I have received several requests to make this pie again.

Recipe was great and tasted even better. I would agree with the others about heating the butterscotch on medium heat in a saucepan. I tried the double boiler option and it was taking forever. Be sure to stir thoroughly though so the butterscotch doesn't over thicken or burn.

I love this pie and I will not buy pudding mix again. The only thing I did different was
I added about a tsp of molasses to cooked
Mixture. It darkened and I did not have to brown in oven

Tasted great. Made it for mother in law for her birthday (her fav). Never had it before, or even had seen one, but made it no problem. The only issue I had was I dont have an 'offical double boiler' I just use a pot of boiling waer with a glass pyrex bowl on top (have used this method for dozens of other double boiler instructions and had no problems). We after stirring forever, I couldnt get it to thicken even before I added my egg. I took it off the double boiler and poured it all in a pot and put it right on the burner. It thickened almost instantly, almost too quick had I not been right there. It turned out perfect. I just couldnt see it even getting hot enough the thicken with the double bolier. TASTED GREAT! Moter in laws eyes bugged out of her head she was so excited!
Good but very sweet. Would reduce the sugar by 1/4c next time. I made stove top (no double boiler) with no problem, just watch closely.
Followed as written and tried to be patient, but even after an hour it refused to thicken. I'll have to try a different recipe and I wish I had heeded the warnings in the reviews

I did not make a pie out of this, HOWEVER, I did fully enjoy the rich, creamy and THICK pudding that this recipe produced...for those who say it was watery and did not set properly, y'all did it wrong, and didn't get it hot enough...you gotta cook the starch or flour long enough for them to soak up the liquid and gelatinize...the amounts of the ingredients will produce a VERY thick filling *shrug*
Stirred as directed for 40 mins, added extra corn startch, extra yolk, and this still would not set. This recipe needs more specific instructions as to ingredients etc.
I use a lot of All Recipes so I was very surprised when this pie did not set. It was a soupy mess. I followed the recipe exactly so I'm not sure what went wrong.

Fantastic taste! Would give the taste 5 stars. I did follow the suggestion to add a teaspoon of molasses since I only had light brown sugar. Only disappointment was my husband said the filling was too skimpy for him next time I'll follow the option for 1-1/2x filling.
My mom had a butterscotch pie recipe but I can't find it. My would never set, so we used spoons and called butterscotch soup. I think this is the recipe. I will be making this this weekend.
